game-self-test: failed — The game didn't save a report with --self-test. montrix took longer than 90 s and was stopped. Give the game a `--self-test <file.json>` option too: start a game the way a player would, drive the player with scripted input for a few seconds, measure from the game's own state whether each step of the core loop works, save the results to that file and exit: {"version": 1, "steps": [{"step": "move", "passed": true, "detail": "walked 3.1 m forward"}, {"step": "act", "passed": true, "detail": "fired 5 shots, 2 hit"}, {"step": "hud", "passed": true, "detail": "health, ammo and the objective are drawn"}]}. "move": the player (or what they steer) moves; "act": their main action works (firing, mining, jumping, eating…); "hud": the on-screen information the original shows (score, health, ammo…) is drawn. Craft Anything runs it after each build, and the game isn't ready until every step passes.
Your open questions: What are Montrix's rules, controls, timing and saved screen? The snapshot container is unsupported by the analysis tools; decode its C64 memory and inspect BASIC/machine code before estimating. (unk_c3be8a6b98faa0d9); Exact runtime fidelity cannot yet be compared: no reference images or original runtime capture, unsupported VICE/6502 in analysis tool and missing Ghidra native decompiler. Manual 6502 decoding is being used. Can the original state be reconstructed with raster, input and sound timing? (unk_2adb88c4b89ecec9). Settle what one more look can and close it with core_unknown_edit (status resolved, the resolution and the evidence ids); say what's left in your summary.
